clue.text: Food constituting a course

definitions.meaning: hard ... is ship's biscuit, and ... is slang for food generally
a sailing ship's ... is the course it holds relative to the wind

explanation.surface: Something to eat that makes up one course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Two unrelated senses of one word: slang for grub, and a ship's heading against the wind.

clue.text: While speaking, man of great intellect is tense

indicators.note: spoken out loud, one word passes for another

parts.note: a titan is a person of great stature or intellect

explanation.surface: A genius talking turns out to be nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to tense a muscle is to tighten it.

clue.text: Trim' coach elaborately, using colour

indicators.note: worked out in an intricate way, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Smarten up a carriage with an ornate paint job.
explanation.definitionFit: Chromatic means relating to or produced by colour.

clue.text: Make an all-out effort hard up on heels of attack

indicators.note: the second piece follows close behind the first, at its heels

parts.note: to go for someone is to attack them
short of money, penniless

explanation.surface: Someone short of cash makes one desperate push right after being attacked.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to risk everything on a single all-out attempt.

clue.text: State for instance replacing one in 7

indicators.note: one piece swaps in for another inside the word

parts.note: the answer to 7 down, the hunter
one as the Roman numeral I
eg is short for exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A state, for example, takes the place of one in seven.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the I of the hunter at 7 for EG.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregon is one of the fifty US states, on the Pacific coast.

clue.text: Instrument played by mother and me

indicators.note: the letters are played about with, rearranged

explanation.surface: A musical instrument performed on by Mum and me.
explanation.definitionFit: An ohmmeter is a measuring instrument for electrical resistance.

clue.text: Be unsure what air-conditioning can do

definitions.meaning: to keep changing one's mind, vacillate
a climate unit can literally send out warm or chilled air

explanation.surface: Indecision compared with an air conditioner's two modes.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for wavering between enthusiasm and indifference, also the literal output of a heating-cooling unit.

clue.text: Hunter soldiers on past island

indicators.note: the word on comes after, beyond, the island

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A huntsman's troops march on beyond an island.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Orion was a giant hunter, later placed among the stars.

clue.text: Record monkey heading off into city in the past

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: the monkey loses its head, the first letter

parts.note: the rhesus is a macaque monkey

explanation.surface: A recorded monkey makes off into a historic city.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephesus was an ancient Greek city in Asia Minor, long since in ruins.

clue.text: First step on the way — for an importunate salesman?

definitions.meaning: an initial advance towards a goal
a pushy doorstep seller literally wedges his shoe in to stop the door closing

explanation.surface: Getting started, as a pushy door-to-door seller does.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for an opening that may lead to more, and literally a doorstep salesman's tactic.

clue.text: Artist, in unfinished sculpture, reflected tall creature

indicators.note: the artist's letters are placed inside the other piece
a reflection shows a thing back to front, so the letters are read in reverse
the word loses its final letter

parts.note: an effigy is a sculpted likeness of a person
RA stands for Royal Academician, a stock crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter stands among a half-made statue, mirrored beside a lofty beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops the last letter of EFFIGY, making EFFIG, which 'reflected' turns into GIFFE. RA (Royal Academician) is a crossword convention for an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: The giraffe is the tallest living animal, an apt description by height.

clue.text: Low European beheaded African

parts.note: to low is to make the sound a cow makes, moo

indicators.note: with its head, the first letter, cut off

parts.note: an Irish person is a European

explanation.surface: A downcast European whose head was cut off, from Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Moorish describes the Moors of north-west Africa, so it is an African adjective.

clue.text: Wristwatch supplies this opportunity for relaxation

definitions.text: Wristwatch supplies this opportunity for relaxation

parts.words: Wristwatch supplies this opportunity for relaxation
parts.note: a watch literally puts the hour on the hands of its face, and the idiom for leisure says the same of the wearer's hands

explanation.surface: An advert claiming a watch gives you a chance to unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: A watch shows the hour by its hands, and a wristwatch sits on a person's hand: both readings of the phrase meet in idle hours.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes spare hours with nothing to fill them, which is a chance to relax.

clue.text: Foolish person, whether from Ulster or not

definitions.text: Foolish person, whether from Ulster or not

parts.words: Foolish person, whether from Ulster or not
parts.note: NI, Northern Ireland or Ulster, put before a word for an idiot still leaves a word for an idiot, so the fool is one with or without that prefix

explanation.surface: A fool, wherever in Ireland he happens to come from.
explanation.walkthrough: NI (Northern Ireland, loosely Ulster) plus TWIT gives the answer, and TWIT alone is also a fool: the clue says the idiot is one with NI or without.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym for a silly, brainless person, much like a twit or a dimwit.

clue.text: Unsettled wife having left, struggles with son

indicators.note: the wife's letter has gone out of the word

parts.note: wrestles means grapples or struggles

explanation.surface: A man left by his wife grapples with his boy and feels unsettled.
explanation.definitionFit: Restless means unable to settle, fidgety and uneasy.

clue.text: Learning from volume about sport

indicators.note: the volume's letters go around the sport

parts.note: an edition is a printed issue of a book
RU is rugby union, a sport

explanation.surface: Knowledge gleaned from a book on games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sport' looks too vague to pin down, but crosswords use RU, rugby union, as their stock sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudition is deep scholarly learning.

clue.text: In twenty-four hundred hours I had almost traversed Montana

indicators.note: the Montana letters reach across, around the rest

parts.note: MT is the postal abbreviation for Montana
contracted to I'd
nigh means nearly or almost

explanation.surface: Someone nearly crosses Montana by the deadline of a full day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' at the start is only a link word; 'twenty-four hundred hours' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: On the twenty-four hour clock, 2400 is twelve o'clock at night.

clue.text: A clock: it could be represented as old-fashioned in America

indicators.note: the letters may be presented again in another arrangement

explanation.surface: A timepiece described as quaintly dated, American-style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be represented' rearranges the letters of A CLOCK IT. An Old Fashioned is a whiskey drink first mixed in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Fashioned is a classic whiskey mixed drink of American origin, so it is one example.

clue.text: Without enough room, set up temporary accommodation around river

indicators.note: the camping word goes around the river

parts.note: camped, pitched a tent for a while

explanation.surface: Squeezed for space, campers pitch tents round a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Cramped means confined, with too little space to move.

clue.text: Stomach —— provide right contents for it

indicators.note: the right letter goes in as the filling for the word meaning provide

parts.note: to endue is to endow or provide with a quality

explanation.surface: A gut needing the proper filling put into it.
explanation.walkthrough: ENDUE is an old verb meaning to supply or endow; R placed in it gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To stomach something is to put up with it, and that is to bear or tolerate it.

clue.text: Political association, one capable of fulfilling wishes for Empress

parts.note: the EU, European Union, is a political association
a genie grants wishes, as in Aladdin

explanation.surface: A political bloc and a wish-granter, offered up for an empress.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugénie was Empress of the French, wife of Napoleon III.

clue.text: A book and a half, describing a stance

annotationWithheld.why: A book and a half, describing a stance (6): A + KIM (Kipling's book) + BO, half of BOOK, so 'book' gives KIM and is also the word halved: one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: A book and a half, describing a stance

clue.text: Naïve kid, lacking refinement, but full of vigour

indicators.note: refining reworks a raw material, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A green youngster, rough around the edges, who is nonetheless bursting with energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' looks like the indicator but is part of the letters; 'refinement' signals the rearrangement of NAIVE KID LACKING.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means thriving and energetic, very much active and vigorous.

clue.text: In Rio, on us the odds are evens

definitions.note: a verb: makes smooth or level

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters, first, third, fifth and so on, are taken

explanation.surface: A bookmaker in Brazil quotes even money on a bet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evens' looks like betting odds, but it is a verb, smooths out.
explanation.definitionFit: To press clothes flat is to smooth or level them out.

clue.text: Have extended look into sharply made point

definitions.note: an imperative: cause something to be lengthened

indicators.note: the look's letters go inside the point

parts.note: a prong is a sharp spike, as on a fork
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Someone takes a long stare at a sharpened tip.
explanation.definitionFit: To lengthen a period or activity is to cause it to be stretched out further in time.

clue.text: Number of motorway I shall return on

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI

indicators.note: returning sends the contraction back the way it came, read in reverse

parts.note: contracted to I'll
taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller vows to come back along a particular motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 (London to Leeds motorway) is read with the figure 1 as letter I, MI. 'return' turns ILL (I'll) into LLI.
explanation.definitionFit: A thousand thousand is a specific large number.

clue.text: Prudence, given fallacious directions

indicators.note: false or misleading, so the letters given are not in their true order

explanation.surface: Caution is advised, since the instructions supplied are misleading.
explanation.definitionFit: Discretion is wise, careful judgement, a synonym of prudence.

clue.text: Work needing joint input

indicators.note: something put in is contained within, so the answer sits inside the first two words

explanation.surface: A task that requires everyone to chip in together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint input' reads as teamwork, but 'joint' is the definition and 'input' says the answer is put inside 'Work needing'.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the hinge joint between thigh and shin.
